introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0760 HISTORY 1, JUNE 2024, ADVANCED LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, Duration: One and a Half Hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the question booklet is headed "Advanced Level - 0760 History 1". Answer ALL the 50 questions in this Examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide on which answer is correct, find the number of the question on the Answer Sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; if you find a question difficult, move on to the next question and come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet, using, where necessary, the blank spaces in the question booklet.
incertitudes: Sujet scanné (CamScanner, filigrane gcerevision.com sans conséquence sur la lisibilité) de 5 pages : page de garde (HISTORY 1, 0760, JUNE 2024, ADVANCED LEVEL, vérifiés), puis 50 QCM sur les pages 2 à 5. Aucun corrigé officiel ni clé imprimée : toutes les réponses sont établies d'après l'historiographie courante, sans source consultable pendant la transcription ; aucun chiffre ni date n'est avancé sans certitude.

Page de garde : le sujet imprime l'instruction 6 « Answer ALL the 50 questions » et l'exemple de marquage ; le numéro de la question 31 est imprimé « 1. » (le chiffre 3 est coupé sur le scan) : lu comme 31 d'après la suite 30, 32. Recopié dans `introduction_markdown` sans les champs administratifs (centre, candidat).
Q33 : le sujet dit « August 1975 » ; le coup d'État qui a renversé Gowon date de juillet 1975 (29 juillet). Date imprimée conservée dans l'énoncé ; réponse A (coup non violent) inchangée.
Q48 : « La Francophonie » est imprimé en italique et avec une majuscule ; recopié sans mise en forme. Q10 : « Indigénat » imprimé en italique, recopié avec l'accent.

Q26 : les options sont défectueuses (aucune ne cite l'aide de la France ou de la Russie à l'Éthiopie ; je n'ai pu confirmer aucun embargo sur les armes contre l'Italie en 1896). Convertie en question ouverte, sans lettre retenue.

Q19 : les quatre options décrivent des mesures qui se défendent comme actions du régime Biya dans les années 1980 (division de la province du Nord en trois en 1983 ; renforcement de la garde présidentielle après 1984) : pas d'exception claire. Convertie en question ouverte, sans lettre retenue. Le détail « dépenses de défense en hausse » n'a pas pu être vérifié par un chiffre.
Q16 : « Train Affair » de 1962 : l'épisode n'a pas pu être vérifié (aucune source consultable) ; la réponse A reste incertaine. Convertie en question ouverte, sans lettre retenue.

Q6, Q32, Q43, Q45, Q47 : plusieurs options se défendent selon la façon de lire le sujet (Q6 « free labour » ou « sexual immorality » ; Q32 langues ou exode des compétences ; Q43 Non-Intervention Committee ou Munich ; Q45 reprise économique de l'Ouest ou expansion soviétique ; Q47 absence d'armée permanente, veto ou finances). Converties en questions ouvertes, sans lettre retenue.

Q18, Q21, Q24, Q29, Q39, Q49 : deux options se défendent ; la réponse la plus conventionnelle est donnée comme « Intended answer » (Q18 B : coût du système fédéral, version officielle, l'option A pétrole étant l'explication critique ; Q21 B ; Q24 B contre C ; Q29 C contre A ; Q39 B contre C ; Q49 B). Converties en questions ouvertes pour autoévaluation.

Réponses retenues avec un degré de certitude moyen (à relire par un historien avant mise en ligne) : Q2 A (chefferie élective : valable pour la plupart des chefferies de la forêt et de la côte, mais les Duala ont une succession héréditaire), Q3 D (but de purification contre conversion ou hégémonie peul), Q7 A (formation d'auxiliaires, l'option D est voisine), Q13 C, Q14 B, Q17 C (le contrôle fédéral des recettes ; l'argument de la viabilité de West Cameroon n'a pas été vérifié), Q28 C (la Seconde Guerre mondiale comme facteur extérieur dominant, mais Pan-Africanisme défendable), Q31 C (retenue par élimination : les autres options sont fausses), Q36 C (D, rejet du Prince de Galles, est un élément du règlement mais pas l'aspiration principale), Q37 A (le chiffre de 130 millions de livres est celui du sujet ; l'ordre de grandeur correspond aux estimations courantes de la dette britannique de 1763), Q50 A (retenue par élimination : les trois autres options sont fausses).

Faits datés cités dans les corrigés, d'après l'historiographie courante : traité germano-duala de juillet 1884 ; campagne du Cameroun 1914-début 1916 ; Troppau 1820 ; Aix-la-Chapelle 1818 ; Corfou 1923 ; Aaland 1921 ; Hot-Line 1963 ; rétablissement des relations avec Israël par le Cameroun en 1986 (rupture en 1973) ; division de la province du Nord en 1983. Aucune citation, statistique ni source inventée.
Défauts d'impression du sujet : pas de clé imprimée ; Q13 et Q17 se terminent par « was because: » (tournure fautive recopiée) ; Q26 options défectueuses ; Q33 date inexacte.
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 6, 16, 18, 19, 21, 24, 26, 29, 32, 39, 43, 45, 47, 49. Aucune clé imprimée sur le sujet.

Coquilles du sujet imprimé conservées ou normalisées : Q29 « the the Mau Mau up-risings » (doublon et trait d'union de fin de ligne, normalisés en « the Mau Mau uprisings ») ; Q37 option C « made England to impose » (recopiée telle quelle).

questions.enonce_markdown: The following were political causes of ethnic movements in Cameroon in the 19th century EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for the cause that was NOT political. Inter-tribal wars (A), feuds between chiefdoms and lineages (B) and the payment of tributes to stronger rulers (C) are all political pressures that pushed groups to leave their homes and move on in the 19th century. The search for pasture (D) is an economic and ecological motive (land for grazing and farming), not a political one, so it is the exception.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: inter-tribal wars.
feuds.
payment of tributes.
the search for pasture.

questions.enonce_markdown: A common characteristic of traditional government in most forest-coastal chiefdoms of pre-colonial Cameroon in the 19th century was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the forest and coastal zone (for example the Bakweri, the Bakundu and the Ejagham or Banyang peoples) the chief was in many cases chosen or confirmed by the kingmakers or the elders on the basis of ability, age and wealth, and not simply inherited the office: chieftaincy was in this sense **elective**. Option C is false because the power of the chief was checked by councils of elders and by secret or regulatory societies (such as Ngbe or Ekpe, and Obasinjom); option D is false for the same reason, since these societies were effective instruments of control; option B, "permanent war clubs", is not a recognised feature of these chiefdoms. Option A is therefore the best answer.

**Answer: A.**
themes: pre-colonial peoples and states of cameroon

choix.texte: the existence of elective chieftaincy.
the existence of permanent war clubs.
the absence of checks and balances.
the ineffectiveness of secret societies.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Jihad was launched in Mandara and Bornu Kingdoms of North Cameroon in the early 19th century mainly to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The jihad that began in Hausaland under Uthman dan Fodio (from 1804) was a reform movement: its leaders accused the rulers of the older Muslim states of mixing Islam with pagan customs and of oppressing their subjects, and they called for the **purification of Islam**. Bornu and Mandara already had Muslim rulers, so the aim could not be to convert their dynasties (B); the liberation of captured Fulani (A) and Fulani domination (C) were at most by-products of the wars. The stated purpose of the jihad was to purify Islamic practices.

**Answer: D.**
themes: fulani jihads in west africa and cameroon

choix.texte: liberate captured Fulani.
convert their ruling dynasties.
impose Fulani hegemony over them.
purify their Islamic practices.

questions.enonce_markdown: A pair that greatly facilitated the evangelisation works of the London Baptist Missionaries in Cameroon in the 19th century was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The missionaries of the Baptist Missionary Society (London), who began work on the Cameroon coast in the 1840s, did not at first speak the local languages. They relied on **local interpreters and catechists** (converts and helpers who translated sermons, taught the new believers and spread the message among their own people) to reach the population. Doctors, naval officers, teachers and craftsmen played a part in the life of the mission stations, but they are not the pair that made evangelisation possible.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: medical and naval officers.
local interpreters and catechists.
teachers and shoe makers.
carpenters and bricklayers.

questions.enonce_markdown: Cameroon became a German protectorate in 1884 following:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The legal basis of the German protectorate was the **Germano-Duala Treaty of July 1884**, signed between the Duala kings (Bell and Akwa and their chiefs) and representatives of German trading firms, after which the German flag was raised by Gustav Nachtigal. His arrival (A) was the means of putting the treaty into effect, not the cause of the protectorate; the Baptist mission left Victoria after the protectorate was established (B); and German plantations (D) were created afterwards.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the arrival of Gustav Nachtigal to the territory.
the sale of Victoria to the Germans by the Baptist missionaries.
the signing of the Germano-Duala Treaty.
the creation of German plantations in the territory.

questions.enonce_markdown:
German administration in Kamerun between 1884 and 1916 was considered 'scandalous' because of:

*Options as printed:* A) deposition of traditional rulers.   B) use of free labour.   C) sexual immorality.   D) introduction of Pax-Germanica.
questions.corrige_markdown:
German rule had a reputation for harshness: forced and unpaid labour on plantations and roads, flogging and other arbitrary punishments, the taking of hostages, and the misconduct of some officials, some of whom were recalled to Germany after scandals. Of the options, "use of free labour" (understood as forced, unpaid labour) and "sexual immorality" (the personal misconduct of some colonial officials) can both be defended as the reason the question has in mind, and the removal of rulers (A) is also a documented policy. The question does not say what is meant by "scandalous", so it cannot be marked reliably as a multiple-choice question.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main reason why the Germans promoted education in Cameroon was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
German education in Kamerun was mainly in the hands of the missions and the government; its practical aim was to produce clerks, interpreters, artisans and teaching assistants who could work for the administration, the trading firms and the plantations, and to spread the German language. The main reason was therefore to **train manpower to serve the Germans**. Reducing unemployment (B) was not a concern of colonial policy, and easing communication among Africans (C) was at best a side effect. Option D, "to promote German administration", is close in meaning but vaguer; the usual formulation of the reason is the training of auxiliaries.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: to train man power to serve them.
to reduce unemployment.
to ease communication among the indigenes.
to promote German administration.

questions.enonce_markdown: German defeat in the First World War in Cameroon was delayed for the following reasons EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The campaign in Kamerun lasted from 1914 until early 1916, much longer than the Allies expected. The Germans resisted for so long because they knew the forests, rivers and mountains well (A), because they could draw on local support and resources in the colony (B), and because their small force was united, organised and disciplined (C). They were not "exhausted by wars of conquest": the colonial conquest had ended years earlier, and the Schutztruppe was not worn out. Option D is not a reason for the delay and is the exception.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: German mastery of the terrain.
domestic support received by the Germans.
German forces were united, organised and disciplined.
German forces were exhausted by wars of conquest.

questions.enonce_markdown: The British policy of Indirect Rule in Cameroon could be criticised in that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Indirect Rule worked through the traditional rulers and their native authorities. Its chief weakness, as the educated Cameroonians pointed out, was that the western-educated **elite were left out of the administration**, which was handed to chiefs who were often illiterate. The other options describe things that Indirect Rule did not do: it did not forbid vernacular languages (B) and it was built on the preservation of local customs and institutions (C); taxation (A) was part of the system rather than the main line of criticism.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the indigenes were compelled to pay taxes.
the use of vernacular was prohibited.
indigenous customs and traditions were ignored.
the elite were neglected in the administration.

questions.enonce_markdown: The policy of Indigénat introduced in French Cameroon during the Mandate era was aimed at:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Indigénat was the French code of special offences for the native population ("indigènes"): it allowed the colonial administrators to punish Africans by imprisonment, fines or forced labour **without any trial**. Teaching French (B) and conversion to French culture (C) belong to the policy of assimilation, and "divide and rule" (D) is a general strategy that is not the specific purpose of the Indigénat.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: inflicting disciplinary penalties without trial on the indigenes.
training Cameroonians to speak the French language.
converting Cameroonians to practice French culture.
dividing Cameroonians so as to rule them.

questions.enonce_markdown: British disrespect for the Trusteeship Agreement was evident in:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Under the Trusteeship Agreement the British had to promote the political, economic, social and educational advancement of the inhabitants of the Southern and Northern Cameroons. In practice they ran the territory as part of Nigeria and neglected its **socio-economic development** (few roads, schools and industries). Law and order were maintained (A), customary law was respected under Indirect Rule (C), and annual reports were sent to the United Nations (D), so these are not signs of disrespect.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the maintenance of law and order.
socio-economic development.
indigenous laws and customs.
submission of annual reports.

questions.enonce_markdown: An important external factor for the rise of nationalism in French Cameroon was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for an **external** factor. The Atlantic Charter (1941), in which the United States and Britain proclaimed the right of peoples to choose their own government, gave the colonised peoples a principle to quote against colonial rule. The returning ex-servicemen (B), the rise in prices (D) and the role of the Church (A) were internal factors, arising inside the territory.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the influence of the Catholic Church.
the influence of ex-service men.
the Atlantic Charter.
the increase in prices of goods.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main factor for the defeat of the UPC in the 1951/52 elections in French Cameroon was because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the elections of 1951 and 1952 the French administration used its power over the voters' lists, the electoral colleges and the counting to favour candidates close to it, notably those of the Bloc Democratique Camerounais (BDC), and to keep the UPC out. The **rigging of the elections** is the main explanation for the UPC defeat. The USCC trade union confederation was close to the UPC and never allied with the BDC (B and A are therefore wrong), and the Bassa-Bamileke quarrel (D) was not the main reason.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the major trade unions turned against the UPC.
the BDC allied with the USCC.
France rigged the elections in favour of the BDC.
of disagreement between the Bassa and Bamileke.

questions.enonce_markdown: Dr. E.M.L. Endeley contributed to his defeat in the 1959 elections because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In 1959 Endeley, leader of the KNC and of the KPP alliance, campaigned for the integration of the Southern Cameroons into Nigeria, which many voters feared as domination by Nigeria. This **pro-Nigeria stance** was his own contribution to his defeat by Foncha's KNDP, which was campaigning for secession from Nigeria and later reunification. He did not adopt a pro-reunification line (A); Grassland solidarity (C) and Foncha's simple image (D) helped the KNDP but are not things that Endeley himself did.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: he adopted a pro-reunification stance.
he adopted a pro-Nigeria stance.
of Grassland solidarity towards the KNDP.
Foncha was simple and associated with the masses.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most cherished ambition of the Southern Cameroons' delegation at the Foumban Conference (1961) was to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
At Foumban (July 1961) the Southern Cameroons delegation led by Foncha wanted a **loose federation** in which West Cameroon would keep wide autonomy and its own institutions, while the East Cameroon delegation under Ahidjo favoured a strong central government. The choice of capital (B), the two official languages (C) and the House of Chiefs (D) were secondary demands compared with the nature of the federation itself.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: secure a loose federation.
make Douala the federal capital.
make English and French official languages.
maintain the House of Chiefs.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Ahmadou Ahidjo's government fell out with the Catholic Church in 1962 because:

*Options as printed:* A) of the 'Train Affair.'   B) it criticized Ahidjo's dictatorship.   C) it collaborated with the UPC terrorists.   D) Ahidjo was a Muslim.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Relations between the Ahidjo government and the Catholic Church were tense in the early 1960s. The printed question refers to a precise episode, the "Train Affair" of 1962, whose details could not be checked in the available sources; the other options are general statements: the personal religion of the president (D) was not in itself a cause of a break, and the accusations of dictatorship (B) and of collaboration with the UPC (C) are the kind of claims that were exchanged between the state and parts of the Church. Because the event behind option A cannot be verified and the other options are not clearly excluded, this question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main reason for the frequent financial difficulties faced by West Cameroon between 1961 and 1972 was because:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Under the 1961 federal arrangements the most productive sources of revenue (such as the main taxes and customs duties) were placed under the **Federal government**, leaving the federated state of West Cameroon dependent on federal grants and on its own limited income, hence the recurrent budget difficulties. Federal subventions did exist, even if they were thought to be insufficient (A); West Cameroon had a productive plantation and farming economy, so the problem was not a lack of viability (B); and the shortage of trained financial staff (D) was a handicap but not the main reason.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: of the absence of federal subventions to the state.
the state was not economically viable.
of its revenue generating sectors being controlled by the Federal government.
of the absence of trained finance personnel to manage the state.

questions.enonce_markdown:
President Ahidjo's establishment of the Unitary State in Cameroon in 1972 was motivated mainly by:

*Options as printed:* A) the discovery of crude oil deposits in West Cameroon.   B) the expensive nature of the Federal System.   C) the need to enhance bilingualism.   D) the need to reunite West and East Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The official justification of the 1972 referendum was that the federal system was too costly (two governments and two assemblies, in addition to the federal ones) and an obstacle to national unity and development, which points to option B. Many Cameroonian historians and critics, however, stress as the real motive the wish of the central government to control the resources of West Cameroon, including the oil that was being discovered off its coast, which points to option A. Because the question says "motivated mainly by" and both explanations are standard, it is not reliable enough to be marked automatically. Option C (bilingualism) was not a motive, and option D (reunification) had already been achieved in 1961.

**Intended answer: B (the expensive nature of the Federal System).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following actions were carried out by the Biya regime to consolidate power in the 1980s EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) increased defence spending.   B) dismissal of Ahidjo's supporters from government.   C) splitting of North Province into three.   D) introduction of rigour and moralisation.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Biya consolidated his position after taking office in 1982 by replacing ministers and officials loyal to Ahidjo (B), by proclaiming the slogan of "rigour and moralisation" (D), and by dividing the vast North Province into three provinces in 1983 (C) so as to reduce the weight of the North. After the failed coup attempt of 1984 the security forces, notably the presidential guard, were also strengthened, which can be presented as increased defence effort (A). All four options therefore describe measures that were in some form part of the policy, and the question has no clear exception, so it cannot be marked reliably as a multiple-choice question.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A major deviation in the foreign policy of Paul Biya from that of Ahmadou Ahidjo was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon had broken diplomatic relations with Israel in 1973 under Ahidjo, like many African states after the Arab-Israeli war of that year. Biya **re-established relations with Israel** in 1986, a clear change from his predecessor. Cooperation with other countries (A), close ties with France (C) and regional cooperation (D) were already features of Ahidjo's policy and were continued, not reversed.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: encouraging international cooperation.
re-establishing relations with Israel.
enhancing diplomatic relations with France.
fostering regional cooperation with neighbouring states.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following factors were both reasons for and impact of the slave trade abolition along the West African coast EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) growth and profitability of legitimate trade.   B) European colonisation of West Africa.   C) establishment of Christian missions in West Africa.   D) poor treatment and massive smuggling of slaves to the New World.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Legitimate trade (A) and the missions (C) are both causes (the economic and humanitarian arguments of the abolitionists) and consequences of abolition. European colonisation (B) was mainly a consequence, used as a justification for intervention, and was not a reason for abolishing the trade in the first place, which makes it the likely exception. However, option D can also be argued as an exception, because the poor treatment of slaves was a reason for abolition while the smuggling that continued was an effect, so it does not fit "both" neatly either. The wording of the question is too loose for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: B (European colonisation of West Africa).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A negative impact of Christian missionary activities on West Africans during the 19th century was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fighting disease (A) and suppressing practices such as human sacrifice or the killing of twins (C) were generally seen as positive results of missionary work, and the changes in trade and agriculture (B) are mixed or economic. The **destruction of African culture** (D), through the condemnation of traditional religion, dances, art and customs, is the negative impact.

**Answer: D.**
themes: christian missionary activity in west africa

choix.texte: fight against the spread of diseases.
significant changes in trade and agriculture.
suppression of evil practices.
destruction of African culture.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most outstanding political impact of the Jihad launched by Uthman Dan Fodio in Hausa land in the early 19th century was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The jihad launched in 1804 led to the creation of the **Sokoto Caliphate**, a large state with Sokoto as capital, governed through emirs who owed allegiance to the Caliph, covering much of northern Nigeria. The overthrow of the Hausa dynasties (B) was a step in this process rather than the outstanding result; trade (C) is an economic and not a political impact; and the region knew many further wars and revolts, so D is not the most outstanding feature.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the establishment of a large Caliphate in Northern Nigeria.
the overthrow of the Hausa ruling dynasties.
the promotion of trade and other economic activities.
the restoration of peace and stability in the region.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The greatest outcome of the Berlin West Africa Conference (1884 - 1885) was:

*Options as printed:* A) the effective occupation of Africa.   B) the passing of the Berlin Act.   C) the creation of the Congo Free State.   D) the growth of African resistance.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The conference, called by Bismarck, ended with the General Act signed on 26 February 1885 (the **Berlin Act**), which laid down rules for the partition: freedom of trade on the Congo and Niger, and the principle that a claim to African territory had to be backed by effective occupation. The creation of the Congo Free State, recognised by the powers at about the same time, is also a major result and could be defended as the "greatest" one by some authors. The principle of effective occupation (A) was set down at Berlin but was only put into practice afterwards, and African resistance (D) was a reaction to the partition. Since B and C are both standard answers, the question is not reliable enough for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: B (the passing of the Berlin Act).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following were evidence that Samori Toure contributed to his own defeat EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks which option is NOT something Samori did himself. His scorched-earth policy as he retreated (A), the enrolment of captives and defeated peoples in his army, whose loyalty could not be relied on (B), and his harsh treatment of conquered peoples, which made them hostile and ready to side with the French (D), were all weaknesses of his own making. The **professionalism of the French soldiers** (C) was a feature of the enemy and not a mistake of Samori, so it is the exception.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: use of scorch-earth policy.
incorporation of captives into his army.
professionalism of French soldiers.
ruthless treatment of defeated people.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An important external factor for the triumph of Abyssinia from Italian imperialism in 1896 was:

*Options as printed:* A) the large size of the Italian army.   B) support from Germany.   C) support from Eritrea.   D) the arms embargo placed on Italy.
questions.corrige_markdown:
At Adowa (1 March 1896) the Ethiopian army of Menelik II defeated the Italians. The usual external factor named by historians is the supply of modern rifles and other help from other European powers, notably France and Russia, which were rivals of Italy; none of the printed options says this. The Italian army was heavily outnumbered, not "large" (A); Germany was Italy's partner in the Triple Alliance and did not support Ethiopia (B); Eritrea was an Italian colony (C); and I could not confirm that any arms embargo was placed on Italy in 1896 (D). The question is defective and cannot be marked as a multiple-choice question.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The educated Africans and nationalists criticised the policy of Indirect Rule because of the following reasons EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The educated elite criticised Indirect Rule because it kept them out of the administration and of the better jobs (A, C) and because it reduced the chiefs to instruments of the colonial government (B). They never criticised it for being "too development-oriented": the usual complaint was the opposite, that the system did little for development and preserved backwardness. Option D is the exception.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: it denied them white collar jobs.
it disrespected traditional rulers.
they were ignored and neglected.
it was too development-oriented.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most important external factor for the rise of African nationalism was:
questions.corrige_markdown:
All four options are external factors, but the **Second World War** is generally treated as the decisive one: African soldiers who served in the Allied armies saw that Europeans could be defeated and were not superior, Britain and France came out of the war economically weakened, and the principles proclaimed in the war (the Atlantic Charter) and the new attitude of the United States and the USSR encouraged the demand for independence. Pan-Africanism (A), the Super Powers (B) and the independence of India and other Asian countries (D) strengthened the movement but came largely as consequences of, or after, the war.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the influence of Pan-Africanism.
the role of the Super Powers.
the Second World War.
the independence of Asian countries.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The Kenyans organised the Mau Mau uprisings in the 1950s against the British with the main objective of:

*Options as printed:* A) achieving self-rule.   B) clamouring for social facilities.   C) the expulsion of white settlers.   D) ending over taxation.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Mau Mau movement, mostly of Kikuyu people, grew out of the loss of land to the white settlers in the highlands; its fighters called themselves the Land and Freedom Army. questions.enonce_markdown:
The greatest failure of Bismarckian Diplomacy was depicted in Germany's:

*Options as printed:* A) inability to secure the friendship of Britain.   B) inability to reconcile Russian and Austrian interests.   C) inability to prevent anti-German alliances.   D) incapacity to keep France perpetually weak.

**Intended answer: B (inability to reconcile Russian and Austrian interests).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The Berlin Blockade of 1948-1949 was a product of:

*Options as printed:* A) American use of the Atomic Bomb.   B) rapid economic growth of the Western zones.   C) Russian encroachment into Western zones.   D) mass migrations from West Berlin.

The Soviet blockade of the Western sectors of Berlin (June 1948 to May 1949) followed the decision of the Western powers to unite their zones of Germany and to introduce a new currency there, which accompanied the economic recovery of the Western zones. This recovery contrasted with conditions in the Soviet zone and worried the USSR, and it is the closest of the options to the usual causes (B). Option C, "Russian encroachment into Western zones", reverses the sequence (the Soviet Union blockaded Berlin, which lay inside its zone, to force the Western powers out), though some textbooks present the blockade as an act of Soviet expansion. The atomic bomb (A) is not a cause, and the migration was from East to West Berlin (D). The question is therefore not reliable enough for automatic marking.
